To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the gravity field is affected by the motion of masses during an earthquake, and (2) the gravity perturbation is a valuable tool for estimating the size of great (magnitude 7 or larger) earthquakes.
the gravity perturbance signals of great earthquakes have been observed and modeled for the first time, opening the window for minute-scale magnitude determination for large earthquakes.

the gravity perturbance signals generated by the Tohoku earthquake are well observed with broadband seismic stations at distances of 1000 to 2000 kilometers and can be modeled accurately by a new formalization that includes both the gravity changes themselves and the gravity-induced motions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the gravity signals generated by the 2011 Tohoku earthquake and their use to estimate the earthquake magnitude.
the detection of gravity perturbations generated by earthquakes.
the detection and interpretation of the gravity perturbatios that occur during an earthquake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors have observed the gravity perturbation signals of the great Tohuko earthquake and modeled them using a new formalism that takes into account both the perturbations in the gravitational field and the gravity-induced motions.
the elastogravity signal has now been observed for a large earthquake and that the modeling is accurate enough to be used for a fast magnitude determination.

the gravity perturbatons are particularly well observed at the distance range between 1000-2000 km from the source of 2011, M9.1 Tohoku earthquake, which is not the same as the distance range of 1000-3000 km mentioned in the abstract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gravity gets into the earthquake prediction game.
the speed of light is the speed of gravity, but gravity is much weaker than the elastic waves.
gravity perturbances are a new tool to estimate earthquake size in real time.

we show that it is possible to observe the gravity perturbation of an earthquake.
gravity perturbances can be observed and used to estimate earthquake magnitudes in real time.
the gravity field perturbations are now well observed, and we have the tools to interpret and model these observations.
